name: agents-md-test-laws-drift
body: AGENTS.md ('Test tiers & the tier-separable harness') cites three global laws that were not authored nodes: `global.constraint.test-tier-boundaries`, `global.constraint.no-real-project-test`, and `global.constraint.self-contained-tests`. The `global` layer held only `build-toolchain-pins`, `checkout-independent-graph-identity`, `frontend-dependency-contract`, and `scan-time-tool-failure-actionable`. [autonomous] I authored all three from the AGENTS.md prose, re-stating `test-tier-boundaries` to the NEW layout (e2e in top-level `tests/`, unit/int in a sibling `tests.rs`, each `#[ignore]`d e2e test carrying the `cargo test-e2e` marker) rather than the retired inline-`mod tests` layout, and authored `behaviour-preserving-refactor` and `decomposition-quality` (the decomposition law, reconciled from the earlier name `module-size-budget` — see `requirements.note.decomposition-reframe-reconciliation`) as the new laws this change-set adds. AGENTS.md remains the prose guide, and it IS a graphed `File` node (`File {fqn:'AGENTS.md'}`, code_type `docs`, lines 1–842; already the `implemented-by` target of `solution.component.repo-agent-guide` and `solution.component.frontend-dependency-docs`), so the plan can schedule the test-tier prose update as a normal graphed-target task — `modifies AGENTS.md`, the `## Test tiers & the tier-separable harness` section (lines 288–397) — with no FQN-less workaround. By contrast, at authoring time `Cargo.toml`, `.cargo/config.toml`, `scripts/gate.sh`, and `apg/config.json` had no `File` node in the branch graph, so their edits were ungraphed config/prose work the plan had to schedule separately. **Correction (present state):** the shipped structural scanner now graphs all four as `File` nodes (`code_type = 'config'`), so edits to them can be scheduled against their FQNs; the AGENTS.md prose update remains a normal graphed-target task.
